text:
Mike (AE): FYI CompanyX sent a detailed identity requirements doc. Key asks: SAML with customer certs (pref RSA-3072), AES-256 assertion encryption, SCIM provisioning for nested groups across two domains, RBAC mapping rules (boolean group logic), and domain ownership proof for multiple domains. They also asked whether Dedicated is mandatory for data residency.

Sarah (ProdSec): Please drop the doc link and I'll start the security questionnaire. Need clarification on cert rotation windows and audit log retention.

Mike (AE): Link pasted to the sales folder (private). Contact is natalie@companyx.com. They require automatic deprovisioning and want token introspection for session validation.

Alex (SE): Two technical notes: 1) nested SCIM groups + automatic deprovisioning is non-trivial on Hosted without a connector. 2) RBAC rules that combine groups (e.g., billing AND admin => super-admin) are supported natively in Dedicated/Private; Hosted needs a mapping layer.

Jia (Eng): We have a SCIM bridge in Redwood Private that handles nested groups. For Hosted we can offer an Okta connector that translates nested groups into flattened role mappings, but it requires an additional enterprise module. Example config snippet for SAML we can share with them: 

```yaml
saml:
  acs_url: "https://companyx-app.redwood.ai/_saml/acs"
  certificate_profile: "rsa-3072"
  encrypt_assertion: true
```

Alex (SE): On Hosted SLOs: introducing a mapping service for RBAC will add an extra call on login provisioning. We should call out 50-150ms median added latency for mapping under typical load.

Ben (Sales): Pricing question from procurement: delta if they require SCIM enterprise + SAML advanced (enc assertions) + Dedicated reserved in two regions. I can run numbers but expect ~1.7-2.0x on top of baseline hosted. I'll draft an indicative term sheet.

Sarah (ProdSec): Immediate blocker: Hosted path needs a short security review to accept encrypted SAML assertions to our control plane. If they insist on AES-256 encrypted assertions to our SaaS, that's an approval item. Dedicated/Private avoids that concern because keys stay customer-controlled.

Mike (AE): They prefer automation, so DNS TXT verification for domain ownership. Also asked about wildcard tenant claims for subdomains.

Jia (Eng): DNS TXT verification is supported. Wildcard subdomain claims are possible but require explicit onboarding mapping for each wildcard pattern; we'll add that to the POC checklist. For SCIM flow: they want Okta -> Redwood provisioning. That's the default connector direction.

Alex (SE): On nested group deprovisioning: we can support cascade deprovision in Private. For Hosted we can demonstrate a connector-based approach in the POC but call out edge cases (overlapping group names across org-scoped namespaces). Recommend we require org-scoped prefixes in mapping (e.g., orgA:team-eng).

Ben (Sales): I'll have a draft SOW + indicative pricing to share by EOD tomorrow.

Sarah (ProdSec): I'll start the questionnaire now. Need the natalie contact on the QA items for cert rotation cadence and if they maintain a dedicated security contact.

Mike (AE): Action list: 
- Ben: SOW + pricing (EOD tomorrow)
- Jia: SCIM connector notes, nested group examples, and mapping templates (Wed)
- Alex: RBAC boolean-rule examples + SLO note for Hosted mapping latency (Wed)
- Sarah: Complete security questionnaire and validate Hosted encrypted assertion path (Tue)

Ben (Sales): noted. Will include options: Hosted + connector (shorter lead) vs Dedicated (longer lead, higher cost, better data isolation).

Natalie (CompanyX): Thanks everyone. Priority is automated lifecycle + strong auditability. We prefer Hosted for a faster POC if assertion encryption can be validated, otherwise we'll need Dedicated. Looking forward to the SOW.

bot-deploy: POC kickoff scheduled: 2025-05-06 16:00 UTC. Invite sent to natalie@companyx.com and Redwood team.

Mike (AE): Perfect. I'll create a calendar invite and loop in legal for the questionnaire execution. :thumbsup:
